speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm. To understand the cause, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and Liver Function Tests. Given your history of heavy smoking, alcohol use, and anabolic steroid use, we need to rule out metabolic derangements, liver toxicity, or potential malignancy as the cause of your progressive weakness and weight loss.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS (Requested Comprehensive Metabolic Panel and Liver Function Tests are not included in the provided data; only Complete Blood Count results are available, which show WBC, Hemoglobin, and Platelets within normal limits).

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work appears normal, but your history of anabolic steroid use, heavy smoking, and unexplained weight loss is concerning. Have you noticed any back pain, radiating pain, or numbness in your legs as well?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The confirmed weight loss of 17 pounds combined with progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, and burning pain is highly concerning for a space-occupying lesion, such as a Pancoast tumor or cervical spine pathology. Have you noticed any changes in your vision or difficulty swallowing?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine with contrast; Chest CT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Chest: Solid mass at the apex of the right lung, suggestive of a tumor; MRI Cervical Spine with contrast: Results not available in provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor). The presence of a solid mass at the apex of the right lung on the Chest CT, combined with your progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, and burning pain, is highly indicative of a tumor invading the lower brachial plexus and cervical sympathetic chain.
